If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (≥0.67 → ≤-0.33) within 2 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% in mid-horizon (days 11–20) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across 5+ consecutive days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in late horizon to avoid flat-outlook overfitting.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3% in early horizon and sentiment is positive, adjust downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon to correct for momentum bias.  
If forecast is below true value by >3% in late horizon and sentiment is negative, adjust upward by 1–2% in early horizon to correct for sentiment-driven underestimation.
